current_episode.title: The Chick-fil-A Strategy Behind This Dealer's Explosive Growth to $1B | Leo Portaluppi, Owner/CEO at P4 Automotive

guest.bio_context: Leo Portaluppi was born in Argentina and moved to the New Jersey area as a young child when his father, a former firefighter, got a job changing oil at a Honda dealership and worked his way up to become a master Honda technician. Leo himself started as a parts runner and porter, then became a Honda technician, service advisor, and eventually a fixed ops manager at around age 26 at a sizable store acquired by the Penske Group. He gained his deeper business education by attending board meetings with Roger Penske, which motivated him to learn every number in the dealership, before seizing an opportunity to become a partner in a small Chrysler store in Kentucky and ultimately building P4 Automotive.

pending_qa.q: What is P4 Automotive's hiring philosophy when it comes to building management talent?
pending_qa.r: Leo Portaluppi's preference is to grow people internally from within the group, both on the sales side and the management side. He summarizes the philosophy with the line 'we don't want to hire bad habits, we want to train bad habits,' though he acknowledges that rapid acquisition growth — four stores in the last 18 months — has forced him to hire externally as he cannot groom internal talent fast enough.

pending_qa.q: How did P4 Automotive's branding as 'Leo' come about, and what did it cost?
pending_qa.r: Leo Portaluppi hired a branding company that conducted months of focus groups, customer surveys, and brand exercises costing $50,000, which concluded he should name the group after himself. Despite initially not wanting his name on the building, he was convinced it was the right move — particularly given the competitive advantage of local identity versus large national dealer groups — and the group website is gotoleo.com.
